Nuclear fuel supply from Russia
*201. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Russia has agreed to supply
nuclear fuel to India from Angarsk
International Uranium Enrichment (AIUE)
Centre set up by it for supply of uranium
to countries with nuclear energy
programmes under International Atomic
Energy Agency safeguards;
(b) whether Government has approved
two nuclear power projects at Rawatbhata
in Rajasthan and Kakrapara in Gujarat  to
be built during Eleventh Plan;
(c) whether fuel supplies facility could
be considered for units being set up through
Russian assistance in the country; and
(d) by when these projects are likely to
start functioning?
Telephone facilities in rural areas
*202. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the revolution in telephones
has not reached the rural areas in the
country inspite of the vast development in
Information Technology;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether the private telephone
operators and even BSNL have failed to
achieve the target for providing telephone
facilities in rural areas in the country; and
(d) if so, the specific steps taken by
Government to take the telephone
revolution to the rural areas in the
country?

64
 Parking policy for Delhi
*203. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL: W ill the Minister of
URBAN DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) the details of the report prepared by
the Delhi Development Authority (DDA)
about the Delhi Government’s parking
policy;
(b) the details of the latest position of
the proposal made with regard to the
establishment of integrated parking under
Government and private participation at
K.G. Marg, Baba  Kharak Singh Marg and
Sarojini Nagar; and
(c) the details of the district centres
falling under DDA’s jurisdiction for which
proposals for multi-storey parkings have
been made by DDA and by when these
multi-storey parkings are likely to be
established?
 Post offices in NER
*204. SHRI O.T. LEPCHA: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of post offices
functioning at present in the rural areas of
North-Eastern Region (NER), particularly
in Sikkim, district-wise;
(b) the number of villages in the States
in NER where post office facility has not
been provided as yet; and
(c) the details of measures taken by
Government to open new post offices in
such villages of  NER?
 Mobile Number Portability
*205. SHRI DARA SINGH:
SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal under
consideration of Government to introduce
a Mobile Number Portability (MNP) in
the four Major metros namely Delhi,
Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata;
(b) whether number portability would
be enabled by a neutral party which would
maintain common database of numbers;
(c) to what extent this proposed move,
including fee likely to be levied for
switching over to another operator while
retaining a mobile number, etc. would be
pro-choice and pro-customer; and
(d) the details thereof?
 Four-laning of Hyderabad-
Vijayawada section
*206. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of SHIPPING,
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Road Safety Forum has
suggested urgent measures to complete the
four-laning of the Hyderabad-Vijayawada
section;
(b) the reasons for delay in this matter;
(c) whether it is a fact that private vested
interests have prevailed over National
Highways Authority of India (NHAI) to
delay development of this section;
(d) whether safety measures would be
introduced immediately on this section; and

(e) the schedule of work on this section
by NHAI and the reasons for delay?
 Notification on the rights of the
forest-dwellers
*207. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR:
Will the PRIME MINISTER  be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government has notified
the provision of right of the forest-dwellers
to the forest land and forest produce in
application of the Act thereon;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?

Availability of uranium in Ladakh
1010. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that scientists
have claimed the availability of uranium in
the ice-covered areas of Ladakh;
(b) whether it is also a fact that after
testing the samples taken from the rocks of
Ladakh areas in the German laboratory,
availability of uranium in heavy quantity
here has been confirmed; and
(c) if so, the extent of time required for
comprehensive information about getting
uranium and starting mining in this area?
Indo-Russian deal in atomic energy
1011. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that an agreement
was signed between India and Russia in the
past months for providing assistance to
generate atomic energy in India;
(b) if so, the date on which this
agreement was signed;
(c) whether talks were held during the
Prime Minister’s recent visit to Russia for
implementation of this agreement;
(d) if so, the facts in this regard;
(e) whether agreement or talks with
other organizations of the world is
necessary for implementation of above
agreement; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
Nuclear Power Plant in Orissa
1012. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:

244
Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(a) whether a site has been identified by
the Centre for setting up a 6,000 mw nuclear
power plant in Orissa;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it would be the largest
nuclear power plant in the country; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Atomic Energy Houses
1013. SHRI PYARELAL
KHANDELWAL: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the proposed Atomic
Energy Houses in the country, State-wise;
(b) whether it is a fact that the case of a
2000 Megawatt capacity Atomic Energy
House in Madhya Pradesh is pending
before Government for approval even after
the declaration of Government in this
regard;
(c) if so, the reasons for delay in the
said approval and by when its approval is
likely to be given; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Allotment of coal blocks
1014. SHRI B.J. PANDA:
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Orissa Government has
asked the Centre for allotment of three coal
blocks for their shell companies created by
State owned Orissa Hydro Power
Corporation;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the time-frame within which the
above proposal of the State Government
would be considered and approved?
Shortage of coal stocks at thermal
stations
1015. SHRIMATI KANIMOZHI: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether thermal stations face severe
shortage of coal stocks;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the remedial action taken to manage
the situation?
Royalty on coal and other minerals
1016. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that States are
facing difficulty as royalty on coal and other
minerals is not revised;
(b) if so, whether State Governments
have demanded that royalty should be
revised;
(c) if so, the decision taken by
Government in this regard; and
(d) whether Government would
compensate for the loss incurred by States
due to non-revision of royalty?
Mining lease applications
1017. MS. MABEL REBELLO: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a large number
of industries whose mining lease
applications have been recommended by
the State Government of Jharkhand to the
Ministry of Coal almost 6 months ago and
his Ministry has not cleared the same;
(b) whether the Ministry has made any
reference to seek clarification from
Jharkhand Government or from the
allottees;
(c) the reasons for the undue delay;

245
(d) the number of such pending cases
which have already been recommended by
the State Government and are waiting to be
cleared by the Ministry; and
(e) the time period taken/required to
clear such projects?
Regulatory authority for coal sector
1018. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to set up a
regulatory authority for coal sector;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
